steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Inflation is a sustained rise in the general price level, measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI). The UK target is 2% CPI inflation. | Key Fact: Demand-pull inflation: too much demand chasing too few goods (e.g. booming economy). Cost-push inflation: rising production costs push prices up (e.g. higher oil prices, wage increases). | Key Fact: Unemployment is when people able and willing to work cannot find jobs. Types: cyclical (recession), structural (skills mismatch), frictional (between jobs), seasonal (tourism, agriculture). | Key Fact: Consequences of inflation: reduces purchasing power (especially for those on fixed incomes), savers lose value, uncertainty discourages investment, and UK exports become less competitive.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain the difference between demand-pull and cost-push inflation, giving a cause of each. | Describe three types of unemployment and explain what causes each. | Evaluate why there may be a trade-off between inflation and unemployment in the short run.
